Tafsir Surat al-Qital

[It is Madani] [[Addition from manuscripts T, M, A.]]

* *

(2739), and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan no. (3715). al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."]].

Thus does Allah set forth for the people their examples﴾, that is, He makes clear to them the final outcome of their deeds and what they will come to in their return.

The Lord, exalted is He, guides the believers to the method they should rely on in their battles with the polytheists: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, [strike] at the necks﴾. That is, when you confront them, mow them down with the swords. ﴿Until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then [secure] the bonds﴾. That is, when you have destroyed them by killing, ﴿then secure the captives﴾ whom you take. Then, after the war has ended and the battle is over, you are free to choose regarding their affair: if you wish, you may show them favour and release their captives without ransom, and if you wish, you may accept ransom from them, taking money from them and sharing it among yourselves.

It is apparent that this verse was revealed after the Battle of Badr, for God, glorified is He, rebuked the believers that day for taking many captives in order to obtain ransom from them, and for killing too few. He said: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives until he inflicts slaughter upon the land. You desire the commodities of this world, but Allah desires the Hereafter. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise. Were it not for a decree from Allah that preceded, you would have been touched for what you took by a great punishment﴾ [al-Anfal: 67–68].

Then some scholars claimed that this verse, which gives the choice between ransoming the captive and releasing him as a favour, has been abrogated (mansukhah, i.e. nullified by later revelation) by the Lord's saying: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and take them, besiege them, and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾ [at-Tawbah: 5]. This was narrated by al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, and it was said by Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and Ibn Juraij.

Others, and they are the majority, said: it is not abrogated.

Then some of them said: the ruler (imam) is only given the choice between showing favour to the captive and ransoming him, and it is not permissible for him to kill him.

Others among them said: rather, he may kill him if he wishes, based on the hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ) killing al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt from among the captives of Badr. And Thumamah ibn Uthal said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he asked him: "What do you have, O Thumamah?" He replied: "If you kill, you kill one who has blood-debt; if you show favour, you show favour to one who is grateful; and if you want wealth, ask and you will be given from it whatever you wish." [Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4372, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, added: the ruler has the choice between killing him, showing favour to him, ransoming him, or enslaving him as well. This question is examined in detail in the science of the branches of jurisprudence (ilm al-furu'), and we have provided proof for this in our book "al-Ahkam" (The Rulings), and all praise and grace belong to Allah.

* *

His saying: ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾. Mujahid said: until 'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) descends. It seems he took this from the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "A group of my nation will continue to prevail upon the truth until their last ones fight the Dajjal." [Reported by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. 2484, from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husain, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Imam Ahmad said: al-Hakam ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Sulaiman, from al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jurashi, from Jubair ibn Nufair, that Salamah ibn Nufail informed them that he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "I have released the horses, laid down the weapons, and the war has laid down its burdens, and I said: 'There is no fighting.'" Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Now the fighting has come. A group of my nation will continue to prevail over the people. Allah will turn the hearts of some people away, so they will fight them, and Allah will provide for them from them, until the command of Allah comes while they are upon that. Verily, the stronghold of the believers is al-Sham, and good is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it likewise through two chains, from Jubair ibn Nufair, from Salamah ibn Nufail al-Sakuni, with the same wording.

Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi said: Dawud ibn Rashid narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Muhajir, from al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jurashi, from Jubair ibn Nufair, from al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, who said: When a victory was granted to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they said: "O Messenger of Allah, the horses have been released, the weapons have been laid down, and the war has laid down its burdens." They said: "There is no fighting." He said: "They have lied. Now the fighting has come. Allah will continue to raise the hearts of a people who fight them, and He will provide for them from them, until the command of Allah comes while they are upon that, and the stronghold of the Muslims is in al-Sham."

Likewise, the hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili narrated it from Dawud ibn Rashid, with the same wording. [Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, no. 1617 (Mawarid), through the chain of Abu Ya'la from Dawud ibn Rashid. Al-Nasa'i narrated it in his Sunan (6/214) through the chain of Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Ablah, from al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jurashi, from Jubair ibn Nufair, from Salamah ibn Nufail, as a marfu' report with similar wording.] The preserved version is that it is from the narration of Salamah ibn Nufail, as previously mentioned. This strengthens the view that there is no abrogation, as though this ruling was legislated for war until there is no war left.

Qatadah said: ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾: until no polytheism remains. This is like His saying: ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 193]. Then some of them said: ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾ means the burdens of those who wage war, namely the polytheists, by their repenting to Allah, mighty and majestic is He. It was also said: the burdens of its people, by their exerting their utmost effort in obedience to Allah, mighty and majestic is He.

* *

That is: this is [the ruling], and if Allah had willed, He would have taken revenge upon the disbelievers with a punishment and chastisement from Him. ﴿But [He ordained fighting] to test some of you by means of others﴾. That is: but He legislated jihad and fighting the enemies for you so that He may test you and examine your conditions. As He mentioned its wisdom in legislating jihad in the two surahs "Al 'Imran" and "Bara'ah" in His saying: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who fought [in His cause] and made evident those who were patient?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 142].

And He said in Surat Bara'ah: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and disgrace them and give you victory over them and satisfy the breasts of a believing people and remove the rage of their hearts. And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills, and Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ [at-Tawbah: 14–15].

Then, since it is among the nature of fighting that many believers are killed, He said: ﴿And those who are killed in the cause of Allah — He will never allow their deeds to be lost﴾. Zayd ibn Yahya al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Ibn Thawban narrated to us, from his father, from Makhul, from Kathir ibn Murrah, from Qais al-Judhami, a man who had companionship (with the Prophet), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The martyr is given six qualities at the first drop of his blood: all his sins are forgiven, he sees his seat in Paradise, he is married to the wide-eyed houris, he is secured from the greatest terror and from the punishment of the grave, and he is adorned with the robe of faith." [Al-Musnad (4/200). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/293): "In its chain is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn Thawban; Abu Hatim and a group considered him trustworthy, and a group weakened him."] Ahmad alone narrated it, may Allah have mercy on him.

Another hadith: Ahmad also said: al-Hakam ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Bahir ibn Sa'id, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from al-Miqdam ibn Ma'd Yakrib al-Kindi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the martyr has six qualities with Allah: he is forgiven at the first gush of his blood, he sees his seat in Paradise, he is adorned with the ornament of faith, he is married to the wide-eyed houris, he is protected from the punishment of the grave, he is secured from the greatest terror, a crown of dignity is placed upon his head, a ruby from which is better than this world and all that is in it, he is married to seventy-two wives from the wide-eyed houris, and he intercedes for seventy of his relatives."

At-Tirmidhi narrated it, and Ibn Majah authenticated it. [Al-Musnad (4/131); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1663; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2799.]

In Sahih Muslim, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr and from Abu Qatadah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Everything is forgiven for the martyr except debt." [Sahih Muslim, no. 1886.] It has been related through the narrations of a group of the Companions. Abu al-Darda' said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The martyr will intercede for seventy of the people of his household." Abu Dawud narrated it. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2522.] The hadiths concerning the virtue of the martyrs are very numerous.

His saying: ﴿He will guide them﴾: that is, to Paradise, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, their Lord will guide them by their faith; beneath them rivers will flow in gardens of pleasure﴾ [Yunus: 9].

His saying: ﴿And He will amend their condition﴾: that is, their affair and their state. ﴿And admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾: that is, He has made them aware of it and guided them to it.

Mujahid said: its people will be guided to their houses and dwellings, and to the places where Allah has allotted them, without error, as though they had been dwelling there since they were created, needing no one to direct them to it.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: They will recognise their houses when they enter Paradise, just as you recognise your houses when you return from the Friday prayer.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: We have been informed that the angel who was assigned to record his deeds in the world walks before him in Paradise, and the son of Adam follows him until he reaches the furthest dwelling that is his, and the angel informs him of everything Allah has given him in Paradise. When he reaches the furthest of his dwellings in Paradise, he enters his dwelling and his wives, and the angel departs from him. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned this, may Allah have mercy on him.

The authentic hadith confirming this has also been reported. Al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Qatadah, from Abu al-Mutawakkil al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the believers are delivered from the Fire, they will be held back at a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, where they will settle the injustices that existed between them in the world. When they have been purified and cleansed, they will be permitted to enter Paradise. By Him in whose hand my soul is, one of them will be more guided to his dwelling in Paradise than he was to his dwelling in the world." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6535.]

Then the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet﴾, like His saying: ﴿And Allah will surely support those who support Him﴾ [al-Hajj: 40]. For the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Therefore He said: ﴿and plant firmly your feet﴾, as came in the hadith: "Whoever conveys to a ruler the need of one who cannot convey it, Allah will make his foot firm upon the Sirat on the Day of Resurrection."

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿And as for those who disbelieve, destruction is theirs﴾. This is the opposite of the firm footing granted to the believers who help Allah and His Messenger ﷺ. It has been established in a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Destroyed is the slave of the dinar, destroyed is the slave of the dirham, destroyed is the slave of the velvet [qatifa] [[Another narration: destroyed is the slave of the cloak (khamisa)]]. He is destroyed and overturned, and if he is pricked, let no one remove the thorn." That is, may Allah not heal him.

Then He said: ﴿The description of the Garden which the righteous have been promised﴾. In a marfu' (traced directly to the Prophet, ﷺ) hadith cited by Ibn Abi Hatim, "unaltered" means: the clear water that has no turbidity in it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, who said: 'Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) said: "The rivers of Paradise gush forth from a mountain of musk."

﴿And rivers of milk whose taste never changes﴾, meaning: rather, it is in the utmost whiteness, sweetness and richness. In a marfu' hadith: "It has not come out of the udders of livestock."

﴿And rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers﴾, meaning: it is not foul in taste and smell like the wine of this world; rather it is pleasing in appearance, taste, smell and effect. ﴿Neither will there be in it any headache, nor will they be intoxicated by it﴾ [al-Saffat: 47]; ﴿They will not be affected by it with headache, nor will they be exhausted﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 19]; ﴿White, delicious to the drinkers﴾ [al-Saffat: 46]. In a marfu' hadith: "Men have not pressed it with their feet."

﴿And rivers of honey clarified﴾, meaning: it is in the utmost purity, beauty of colour, taste and scent. In a marfu' hadith: "It has not come out of the bellies of bees."

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, al-Jurayri informed us, from Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "In Paradise there is a sea of milk, a sea of water, a sea of honey, and a sea of wine; then the rivers branch out from them afterwards."

[[Abu Nu'aym also related it in Sifat al-Jannah no. (314) via Mu'alla ibn Asad from al-Harith ibn 'Ubayd with it.]]

In the Sahih: "When you ask Allah, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle and highest of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful." [[The hadith's takhrij was previously mentioned at the tafsir of verse 133 of Surah Al 'Imran.]]

They are not alike; that is, the one in the ranks (of Paradise) is not like the one in the depths (of Hell). ﴿And they are given boiling water to drink﴾, meaning: water that is hot, of intense heat, unbearable. ﴿So it cuts their intestines to pieces﴾, meaning: it severs what is in their bellies of intestines and entrails, we seek refuge with Allah from that.

He says: ﴿Is one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord﴾, meaning: upon insight and certainty regarding the command of Allah and His religion, through what Allah has sent down in His Book of guidance and knowledge, and through the upright natural disposition (fitrah) with which Allah has created him, ﴿like one for whom the evil of his deeds has been made attractive, and who follow their desires?﴾ Meaning: this is not like that. It is like His saying: ﴿Is one who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 19], and like His saying: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of the Garden are not equal. The companions of the Garden are the ones who are triumphant﴾ [al-Hashr: 20].

Then He said: ﴿The description of the Garden which the righteous have been promised﴾. Ikrimah said: ﴿The description of the Garden﴾, meaning its attributes [[In T, M, A: "its delights."]]: ﴿therein are rivers of water unaltered﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: meaning not changed. Qatadah, al-Dahhak and 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: not foul-smelling. The Arabs say: "The water became āsin" when its smell changed.

In a marfu' (traced directly to the Prophet, ﷺ) hadith cited by Ibn Abi Hatim, "unaltered" means: the clear water that has no turbidity in it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, who said: 'Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) said: "The rivers of Paradise gush forth from a mountain of musk."

﴿And rivers of milk whose taste never changes﴾, meaning: rather, it is in the utmost whiteness, sweetness and richness. In a marfu' hadith: "It has not come out of the udders of livestock."

﴿And rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers﴾, meaning: it is not foul in taste and smell like the wine of this world; rather it is pleasing in appearance, taste, smell and effect. ﴿Neither will there be in it any headache, nor will they be intoxicated by it﴾ [al-Saffat: 47]; ﴿They will not be affected by it with headache, nor will they be exhausted﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 19]; ﴿White, delicious to the drinkers﴾ [al-Saffat: 46]. In a marfu' hadith: "Men have not pressed it with their feet."

﴿And rivers of honey clarified﴾, meaning: it is in the utmost purity, beauty of colour, taste and scent. In a marfu' hadith: "It has not come out of the bellies of bees."

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, al-Jurayri informed us, from Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "In Paradise there is a sea of milk, a sea of water, a sea of honey, and a sea of wine; then the rivers branch out from them afterwards."

His saying: ﴿So know that there is no deity except Allah﴾. This is an informing that there is no deity except Allah, and it does not conflict with His being one who commands knowledge of this. For this reason He follows it with His saying: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin, and for the believing men and believing women﴾. And in the Sahih it is reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "O Allah, forgive me my wrongdoing and my ignorance, my excess in my affairs, and what You know better than I. O Allah, forgive me my jest and my earnestness, my errors and my deliberate faults, and all of that is with me." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6398.] And in the Sahih that he used to say at the end of the prayer: "O Allah, forgive me what I have done before and what I have done later, what I have concealed and what I have made public, my excess, and what You know better than I. You are my God; there is no deity except You." [Sahih Muslim, no. 769.] And in the Sahih that he said: "O people, repent to your Lord, for I seek forgiveness from Allah and turn to Him more than seventy times a day." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6307.]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Sarjis say: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and ate with him from his food. I said: "May Allah forgive you, O Messenger of Allah." Then I said: "Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ask forgiveness for you?" He said: "Yes, and for you as well," and he recited: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin, and for the believing men and believing women﴾. Then I looked at the bone of his right shoulder blade, or his left shoulder blade (Shu'bah, who doubted), and there it was like a gathering, with warts upon it.

Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through various chains, from Asim al-Ahwal, with this wording. [Musnad Ahmad (5/82); Sahih Muslim no. 2346; al-Shama'il of al-Tirmidhi no. 22; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 11496.]

In another hadith narrated by Abu Ya'la: Muharrar ibn Awn narrated to us, Uthman ibn Mattar narrated to us, Abd al-Ghafur narrated to us, from Abu Nasirah, from Abu Raja', from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hold fast to 'There is no deity except Allah' and seeking forgiveness, and multiply them both, for Iblis said: 'I destroyed people through sins, and they destroyed me through "There is no deity except Allah" and seeking forgiveness. When I saw that, I destroyed them through desires, and they think they are guided.'" [Musnad Abu Ya'la (1/123). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/207): "In it is Uthman ibn Mattar, who is weak."]

And in the narration reported: "Iblis said: 'By Your might and Your majesty, I will not cease misleading them as long as their souls are in their bodies.' Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: 'By My might and My majesty, I will not cease forgiving them as long as they ask My forgiveness.'" [Ahmad in his Musnad (3/29), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him).]

The hadiths on the virtue of seeking forgiveness are very numerous.

His saying: ﴿And Allah knows your moving about and your resting place﴾, meaning: He knows your activity during your day and your dwelling place during your night, like His saying: ﴿And it is He who takes you back at night and knows what you have committed by day﴾ [Al-An'am: 60], and like His saying: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon Allah, and He knows its place of rest and its place of storage; all is in a clear record﴾ [Hud: 6]. This view was held by Ibn Juraij, and it is the preference of Ibn Jarir. And from Ibn Abbas: your moving about in this world, and your resting place in the Hereafter.

The first is more fitting and more apparent, and Allah knows best.

Allah the Exalted says, informing about the hypocrites and their dullness and poor understanding: they would sit with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), listen to his speech, and understand nothing from it. When they left his presence, ﴿they said to those who had been given knowledge﴾ from among the Companions: ﴿"What did he just say?"﴾ meaning: just now. They did not comprehend what was being said, and they paid it no attention.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has sealed, and who follow their desires﴾, meaning: there is no sound understanding in them, and no sound intention.

Then He said: ﴿But those who are guided, He increases them in guidance﴾, meaning: those who sought guidance, Allah granted them success in it, guided them to it, kept them firm upon it, and increased them in it. ﴿And He grants them their taqwa﴾, meaning: He inspires them with their right guidance.

* *

His saying: ﴿So are they waiting for anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly?﴾ meaning: while they are heedless of it. ﴿Its signs have already come﴾, meaning: the indications of its approach, like His saying: ﴿This is a warner of the warners of old. The approaching [Hour] has approached﴾ [An-Najm: 56-57], and like His saying: ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split﴾ [Al-Qamar: 1], and His saying: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ [An-Nahl: 1], and His saying: ﴿The reckoning of men has drawn near to them, while they are in heedlessness, turning away﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 1]. Thus the sending of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is one of the signs of the Hour, because he is the Seal of the Messengers, through whom Allah perfected the religion and established the proof upon all the worlds. He (ﷺ) informed about the signs of the Hour and its indications, and clarified and explained them in a way that no Prophet before him was given, as is expounded in its proper place.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The sending of Muhammad (ﷺ) is one of the signs of the Hour. And that is as he said. For this reason it came in his names (ﷺ) that he is the Prophet of Repentance, the Prophet of the Great Battle, the Hashir (the one at whose feet people will be gathered), and the Aqib (the last one after whom there is no Prophet).

Al-Bukhari said: Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, Fudayl ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Abu Hazim narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gesture with his two fingers like this, the middle finger and the one next to it, and say: "I and the Hour have been sent like these two." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4936.]

Then He said: ﴿So how will they have their reminder when it comes to them?﴾ meaning: how will the disbelievers benefit from remembrance when the Resurrection comes upon them, when such remembrance will not benefit them? Like His saying: ﴿On that Day man will remember, but how will remembrance benefit him?﴾ [Al-Fajr: 23], and ﴿And they will say, "We believe in Him." But how can they reach [faith] from a far place?﴾ [Saba: 52].

O Allah, forgive me my jest and my earnestness, my errors and my deliberate faults, and all of that is with me." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6398.] And in the Sahih that he used to say at the end of the prayer: "O Allah, forgive me what I have done before and what I have done later, what I have concealed and what I have made public, my excess, and what You know better than I. You are my God; there is no deity except You." [Sahih Muslim, no. 769.] And in the Sahih that he said: "O people, repent to your Lord, for I seek forgiveness from Allah and turn to Him more than seventy times a day." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6307.]

The Most High says, informing about the believers, that they wished for the legislation of jihad (holy struggle). When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prescribed it and commanded it, many people shrank back from it [[In T: "Allah Ta'ala".]], as in His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands, establish the prayer and give the zakah"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a party of them fear men as they should fear Allah, or with even greater fear, and they say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You would delay us to a near term." Say: "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged a whit."﴾ [An-Nisa 4:77].

Here He says: ﴿And those who believed say, "If only a surah were sent down."﴾ That is, a surah containing the ruling on fighting. Therefore He said: ﴿But when a decisive surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the look of one fainting from death.﴾ That is, from their fright, their terror and their cowardice before meeting the enemy. Then He said, encouraging them: ﴿Obedience and fair speech would be better for them.﴾ That is, it would have been more fitting for them to listen and obey, in the present situation. ﴿And when the matter is resolved upon﴾ means the situation becomes serious and fighting arrives. ﴿Then if they had been true to Allah﴾ means if they had made their intention sincere toward Him, ﴿it would have been better for them.﴾

And His saying: ﴿Then would it be that if you turned away, you would cause corruption on earth and sever your ties of kinship?﴾ That is, if you turned away from jihad and shrank back from it.

That is, you would return to what you were in of the utter ignorance (al-jahiliyyah, the pre-Islamic age of ignorance), shedding blood and severing the ties of kinship (al-arham). Therefore He said: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He has made them deaf and blinded their vision.﴾ This is a prohibition against corruption on earth in general, and against severing kinship in particular. Indeed, Allah Ta'ala has commanded righteousness on earth and the maintaining of kinship (silat al-arham), which is kindness to relatives in speech and deeds and the giving of wealth. Authentic (sahih) and good (hasan) hadiths on this have been related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) through many routes and in many forms.

Al-Bukhari said: Khalid ibn Makhlad related to us, Sulayman related to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Muzarrid related to me, from Sa'id ibn Yasar [[In T: "Al-Bukhari related with his chain".]], from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah created the creation, and when He finished with it, the womb (ar-rahim) stood up and seized hold of the lap of the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic. He said: 'Enough!' It said: 'This is the station of one who seeks refuge in You from severing.' He said: 'Are you not pleased that I join whoever joins you, and sever whoever severs you?' It said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then that is yours.'" [[In A: "Then that is for you".]] Abu Hurairah said: Recite if you wish: ﴿Then would it be that if you turned away, you would cause corruption on earth and sever your ties of kinship?﴾ [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4830.]].

Then al-Bukhari related it through two other routes, from Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Muzarrid, with the same wording. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Recite if you wish: ﴿Then would it be that if you turned away, you would cause corruption on earth and sever your ties of kinship?﴾" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4831, 4832, but Abu al-Hubab added between Mu'awiyah and Sa'id ibn Yasar.]] Muslim also related it from the hadith of Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Muzarrid, with the same wording [[Sahih Muslim, no. 2554, through the route of Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Muzarrid from his paternal uncle Abu al-Hubab from Sa'id ibn Yasar with the same.]].

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il related to us, 'Uyaynah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jawshan informed us, from his father, from Abu Bakrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no sin more deserving that Allah hastens its punishment in this world, along with what is stored up for its doer in the Hereafter, than rebellion (al-baghy) and severing the ties of kinship."

It was related by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Isma'il (i.e., Ibn 'Ulayyah), with the same [[Al-Musnad (5/38), Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4902, Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2511, Sunan Ibn Majah no. 4211.]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a sahih hadith.

Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Bakr related to us, Maymun Abu Muhammad al-Mar'i related to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abbad al-Makhzumi related to us, from Thawban, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever is pleased that his provision be increased and his life be extended, let him maintain his ties of kinship" [[Al-Musnad (5/279). Its corroboration is the hadith of Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), marfu': "Whoever wishes that his provision be expanded for him, or his life be prolonged, let him maintain his ties of kinship." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 5986, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2557, the wording being Muslim's.]]. Ahmad alone related it, and it has a corroboration in the Sahih.

Ahmad also said: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, Hajjaj ibn Artah related to us, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have relatives (dhawu arham). I maintain ties with them and they sever them; I forgive them and they wrong me; I do good to them and they do evil to me. Shall I repay them?" He said: "No, for then you will all be left [to ruin]. Rather, give them of your bounty and maintain ties with them, for there will always be with you a helper from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as long as you remain upon that" [[Al-Musnad (2/181).]].

Ahmad alone related it through this route, and it has a corroboration through another route [[In A: "corroborations".]].

Imam Ahmad said: Ya'la related to us, Fitr related to us, from Mujahid, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr [[In T: "from Ibn 'Umar".]], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the womb is suspended from the Throne, and the one who maintains ties is not the one who merely repays [in kind]; rather, the one who maintains ties is the one who, when his ties are severed, joins them." Al-Bukhari related it [[In T: "He alone related it".]] [[Al-Musnad (2/163), Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5991.]].

Ahmad said: Bahz related to us, Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, Qatadah informed us, from Abu Thumamah al-Thaqafi, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection the womb will be placed, having a hook like the hook of a spindle, speaking with an eloquent and clear tongue, and it will join whoever joined it and sever whoever severed it" [[Al-Musnad (2/189). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/150): "The men of Ahmad are the men of the Sahih, except Abu Thumamah al-Thaqafi, whom Ibn Hibban declared trustworthy."]].

Show mercy to those on earth, and the one in heaven will show mercy to you. The womb is a branch from the Most Merciful; whoever joins it, Allah joins him, and whoever severs it, Allah severs him."

It was related by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi [[In T: "Ahmad and Abu Dawud related it".]] from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, with the same [[Al-Musnad (2/160), Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4941, Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 1924.]]. I created the womb and derived for it a name from My name. Whoever maintains it, I will maintain him, and whoever severs it, I will sever him, cutting him off entirely'" [or he said: "whoever cuts it off, I will cut him off"].

He alone related it through this route [[Al-Musnad (1/191).]]. Ahmad also related it from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from al-Radad, or Abu al-Raddad, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, with the same [[Al-Musnad (1/194). Al-Tirmidhi said in the Sunan: "Ma'mar related this hadith from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Radad al-Laythi, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf. Muhammad [i.e., al-Bukhari] said: the hadith of Ma'mar is erroneous." The sound narration is the one that follows in the Sunan.]]. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/287): "It contains a group whom I do not know." It has a corroboration from the hadith of Abu Hurairah related by Ahmad in al-Musnad (2/295).]].

And with this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When speech becomes manifest, deeds are stored away, tongues are united [in falsehood], hearts hate one another, and every person of kinship severs his kin, then Allah curses them, makes them deaf, and blinds their vision" [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/263), and the discussion of it is as for the preceding.]].

So this was revealed: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not nullify your deeds﴾, and they feared that sin would nullify deeds.

Then it was narrated through the chain of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak: Bukayr ibn Ma'ruf informed me, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: We, the company of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, used to consider that no good deed was rejected, until this was revealed: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not nullify your deeds﴾. So we said: What is this that nullifies our deeds? We said: the major sins that necessitate punishment and the grave immoralities, until this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be set up with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [An-Nisa': 48]. When it was revealed, we refrained from speaking about that, and we feared for those who committed major sins and grave immoralities, and we hoped for those who did not commit them. [[Ta'zim qadr al-salah lil-Marwazi, nos. (698, 699).]]

Then Allah commanded His believing servants to obey Him and obey His Messenger, which is their happiness in this world and the Hereafter, and forbade them from apostasy, which nullifies deeds. Therefore He said: ﴿and do not nullify your deeds﴾, meaning: by apostasy. For this reason He said after it: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and barred others from the way of Allah, then died while they were disbelievers, Allah will never forgive them﴾, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be set up with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾, and so on.

Then He said to His believing servants: ﴿So do not weaken﴾, meaning: do not become feeble before the enemies, ﴿and call to peace﴾, meaning: to truce and reconciliation, and laying down fighting between you and the disbelievers while you are in a state of strength and large numbers and equipment. Therefore He said: ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace while you are the superior ones﴾, meaning: while you are in a state of superiority over your enemy. As for when the disbelievers have strength and numbers relative to all the Muslims, and the Imam sees a benefit in a covenant and truce, then he may do that, just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did when the disbelievers of Quraysh barred him from Makkah, and called him to reconciliation and laying down war between them and him for ten years, and he agreed to that.
